items.title: Stock Radar: Breakout from bullish pennant pattern makes Deepak Nitrite an attractive buy
items.description: Deepak Nitrite Ltd has broken out from a bullish pennant pattern on daily charts, signaling potential for further upside. Experts suggest short-term traders can target Rs 1,900 in the next 2-3 weeks, with a stop loss below Rs 1,760. The stock has shown strong recent performance and a bullish technical setup.

items.title: SBI shares in focus ahead of Q4 results; lender set to consider up to $2 billion fundraising plan on May 12
items.description: State Bank of India's board will consider a fundraising plan of up to $2 billion on May 12. The bank will also release its Q4 results today, with analysts expecting muted profit growth due to treasury losses, despite stable loan growth and margins. SBI shares have seen significant gains over the past year.

items.title: Polycab India among 3 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On May 7, three stocks from the Nifty 200 segment appeared on the White Marubozu bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern that forms when the opening price is the lowest, and the closing price is the highest for the session.It is represented by a long bullish candlestick with little to no shadows, indicating strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a sign that buyers dominated from open to close, often using it to identify potential continuation of upward price trends.

items.title: KPIT Technologies among 5 F&O stocks with a sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of May 07, five stocks in the NSE F&O pack saw a notable surge in futures open interest, contributing to a total increase in open interest of over 10% compared with the previous trading session. A significant uptick in futures open interest signifies substantial growth in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a specific security. This uptrend reflects an increasing number of participants either initiating new positions or expanding the size of their existing positions in the futures market.

items.title: Pidilite Industries shares in focus after Q4 net profit jumps 37% to Rs 584 crore, revenue rises 14%
items.description: Pidilite Industries reported a 36.6% year-on-year jump in Q4FY26 net profit to Rs 584.2 crore, with revenue rising 14.1%. Margin expansion was driven by lower input costs. The company also posted steady full-year growth, supported by strong performance in its Consumer and Bazaar segment and stable demand conditions.

items.title: Dabur shares in focus as Q4 net profit rises 15% to Rs 369 crore, revenue up 7.3%
items.description: Dabur India reported a 15% year-on-year rise in Q4FY26 net profit to Rs 369 crore, with revenue increasing 7.3%. Growth was driven by strong domestic FMCG performance and volume expansion. However, profits declined sequentially. The company also saw broad-based category growth and modest international business expansion.

items.title: Hero MotoCorp among 7 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: Seven stocks from the Nifty500 segment were identified in the RSI Trending Up scan on May 7, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. “RSI trending up” indicates strengthening price momentum, which may signal potential upward movement and help traders spot buying opportunities.

items.title: OnEMI Technology shares to list today. GMP signals at one of the strongest debuts in recent past
items.description: OnEMI Technology Solutions, the company behind Kissht, is poised for its stock market debut. Grey market trends suggest a strong listing, with shares expected to trade above the issue price. The IPO saw significant demand, particularly from institutional investors. Proceeds will bolster the company's NBFC subsidiary for future loan growth. Investors anticipate a successful debut for this fintech player.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 8 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, 16 stocks closed above their 200-day moving average (DMA) on May 7, 2026, according to technical scan data from StockEdge. Among these, we have highlighted the top eight stocks that posted gains of more than 3%. The 200-day daily moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend in a particular stock. As long as the stock is priced above the 200-day SMA on the daily timeframe, it is generally considered to be in an overall uptrend. Take a look:

items.title: Trendline Breakout Points to Bullish Reversal in Deepak Nitrite
items.description: “Deepak Nitrite stock had witnessed a phase of consolidation after which it has recently given a breakout surpassing its previous hurdle of 1780 levels. Traders can buy for a target of Rs 1900 in the next 2-3 weeks,” Shivangi Sarda, Analyst, Derivatives and Technical Research, Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, said.

items.title: Dalal Street likely to open in red amid weak GIFT Nifty cues
items.description: Indian stock markets saw a mixed trading day on May 7. The Sensex experienced volatility due to its weekly expiry. Analysts suggest a breakout above 24,400 could lead to further gains. India VIX, a measure of market fear, declined significantly. Foreign and domestic investors were net buyers of shares.

items.title: Stocks in news: SBI, Titan, Hyundai, BSE, Torrent Pharma, Axis Bank
items.description: Indian markets saw volatile trading on Thursday, closing nearly unchanged despite positive signals. Several companies including SBI, Titan, and Hyundai are in focus today. Many firms will announce their fourth-quarter results. Britannia Industries reported strong profit growth and recommended a dividend. BSE also posted a significant profit surge. Bharat Forge's profit declined, while Dabur India saw a profit uptick.

items.title: Midcap rally hits record high amid retail buying surge
items.description: Nifty midcap indices reached new peaks on Thursday. This surge is fueled by robust earnings, consistent retail investor contributions, and strategic bargain purchases. Midcap and smallcap indices have significantly outperformed larger indices since the US-Iran ceasefire announcement a month ago. Experts suggest a pause in the rally is likely soon. Foreign investors have been selling large-cap stocks.

items.title: Foreign investors continue to pull out of financials in second half of April
items.description: Foreign investors continued their sell-off in Indian equities, particularly in financials, extending withdrawals into the latter half of April. This sector saw significant outflows due to its heavy weight and inflation concerns. Conversely, power and capital goods attracted substantial inflows, driven by strong demand and global trends.

items.title: Retail stake cut in 284 BSE 500 companies in Q4
items.description: Retail investors showed caution, reducing their stock holdings in most companies during the March quarter. This move coincided with market declines due to global uncertainties. Meanwhile, foreign investors and domestic funds increased their stakes in various companies. Promoters also raised their shareholding, taking advantage of lower stock prices. FPI stake in Indian companies continued to fall.

items.title: Foreign remittances to Kerala stay resilient despite West Asia crisis
items.description: Money from non-resident Indians to Kerala remains strong. Banks like Federal Bank and South Indian Bank show growth in deposits. This inflow is vital for Kerala's economy. A weaker rupee also boosts remittances. Experts believe inflows will continue unless job losses in the Middle East occur. A prolonged conflict could pose a long-term risk.
